{{Short description|French mathematics research institute}}
{{Infobox institute|name=Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu – Paris Rive Gauche|image=[[File:Logo_IMJ-PRG.png]]|parent=[[CNRS]], [[Sorbonne University]], [[Paris Cité University]]|established=1994|focus=Fundamental mathematics|head=David Hernandez|staff=200 permanent research, 500 total|location=|city=[[Paris]]|country=[[France]]|coor={{coord|48.826906|2.380329}}|website=https://www.imj-prg.fr}}

The '''Mathematics Institute of Jussieu–Paris Rive Gauche''' ({{langx|fr|Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu–Paris Rive Gauche}}, {{IPA|fr|ɛ̃stity də matematik də ʒysjø paʁi ʁiv ɡoʃ|pron}}, '''IMJ-PRG''') is a French research institute in [[Pure mathematics|fundamental mathematics]]. It is a "mixed research unit", with three parent organizations: the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]], [[Sorbonne University]], and the [[University of Paris (2019)|University of Paris]]. It is located in [[Paris]], split between two campuses: [[Jussieu Campus|Jussieu]] and [[Paris Rive Gauche]].

It is the largest research center for fundamental mathematics in [[France]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hceres.fr/content/download/32603/497683/file/D2019-EV-0751723R-DER-PUR190015906-024200-RF.pdf|title=Évaluation de l'unité : Institut de Mathématiques de Jussieu-Paris Rive Gauche|last=Haut Conseil de l'évaluation de la recherche et de l'enseignement supérieur|authorlink=|date=|website=hceres.fr|language=French|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180917215427/http://www.hceres.fr/content/download/32603/497683/file/D2019-EV-0751723R-DER-PUR190015906-024200-RF.pdf|archive-date=2018-09-17|access-date=2018-08-22|url-status=dead}}</ref> More than 200 permanent researchers work at the institute, around 100 PhD students, as well as [[Emeritus|emeritus professors]], postdocs, invited researchers, and ATERs, and support staff.

The IMJ-PRG is the largest research unit linked to the [[doctoral school]] of mathematical sciences of Paris center (''École doctorale de sciences mathématiques de Paris-Centre''). It has its own [[Academic journal|journal]], the ''Journal de l'institut de mathématiques de Jussieu'', published by [[Cambridge University Press]] and covering all areas of fundamental mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-institute-of-mathematics-of-jussieu|title=Journal of the Institute of Mathematics of Jussieu {{!}} Cambridge Core|website=Cambridge Core|language=en|access-date=2018-09-22}}</ref>

Each year since 2001, the institute organizes an international [[summer school]] dedicated to a hot topic in current mathematical research.

== History ==
The institute was created on January 1, 1994, under the name ''Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu''. It moved in 1999 to the Chevaleret location in Paris. In 2010, half of the institute moved back to Jussieu; in 2013, the other half moved to Paris Rive Gauche and the institute changed its name to the current one.

The institute is one of the founding members of the [[Research Federation in Mathematics of Paris Center]] (''Fédération de recherche en mathématiques de Paris centre''). Since 2007, it has been affiliated with the [[Mathematical Sciences Foundation of Paris]] (''Fondation sciences mathématiques de Paris'').

The directors of the Institute were successively: Christian Peskine (1994-2000), Harold Rosenberg (2000-04), Gilles Godefroy (2004-08), [[Håkan Eliasson]] (2008-12), Patrice Le Calvez (2012-16), [[Loïc Merel]] (2016-21), Olivier Biquard (2021-25), David Hernandez (2026-).{{citation needed|date=May 2026}}

=== Distinctions ===
Several members of the IMJ-PRG received national and international awards for their research.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imj-prg.fr/spip.php?rubrique91&lang=fr|title=Prix et distinctions|last=IMJ-PRG|date=|website=www.imj-prg.fr|language=fr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612140507/https://www.imj-prg.fr/spip.php?rubrique91&lang=fr|archive-date=2018-06-12|access-date=2018-06-09|url-status=dead}}</ref> Most prominently, [[Artur Avila]] received the [[Fields Medal]] in 2014,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/alexs-adventures-in-numberland/2014/aug/13/fields-medals-2014-maths-avila-bhargava-hairer-mirzakhani|title=Fields Medals 2014: the maths of Avila, Bhargava, Hairer and Mirzakhani explained|date=2014-08-13|website=the Guardian|language=en|access-date=2018-06-09}}</ref>, [[Claire Voisin]] received the [[CNRS Gold medal]] in 2016,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.cnrs.fr/articles/claire-voisin-2016-cnrs-gold-medal|title=Claire Voisin, 2016 CNRS Gold Medal|website=CNRS News|language=en|access-date=2018-06-09}}</ref>,  and [[Michel Talagrand]] received the [[Abel prize]] in 2024<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://abelprize.no/citation/citation-michel-talagrand|title=Citation - Michel Talagrand}}</ref>.

== Themes ==
The research at the IMJ-PRG covers most of fundamental mathematics. It is subdivided in twelve team-projects: [[algebraic analysis]]; [[complex analysis]] and [[complex geometry|geometry]]; [[functional analysis]]; [[operator algebra]]; [[combinatorics]] and [[optimization]]; [[automorphic form]]s; [[history of mathematics|history of mathematical sciences]]; geometry and [[dynamical system|dynamics]]; [[Group (mathematics)|groups]], [[Representation theory|representations]], and [[Geometric group theory|geometry]]; [[mathematical logic]]; [[number theory]]; and [[algebraic topology]] and [[algebraic geometry|(algebraic) geometry]].
